prev: 28 Feb 2026 — US Operation Epic Fury began alongside Israel's campaign; Iran's Supreme Leader was killed. A naval blockade followed and the Strait of Hormuz has not returned to normal traffic since.
7 Aug — Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey signed the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement. Turkey's parliament has not ratified it.

23–25 Sep — Zelenskyy said Ukraine is ready for an energy-only ceasefire and asked for a trilateral meeting with Putin and Trump; Russia has not agreed. A 295-drone Russian barrage on Kyiv killed seven on the 25th.

24–25 Sep — Houthi missile and drone salvos on Riyadh and Saudi Aramco facilities; the three Mecca Pact military chiefs were summoned to urgent talks in Riyadh. Neither Pakistan nor Turkey has committed combat forces, and Washington has refused Saudi requests for US strikes on the Houthis.

25 Sep — Iran put its terms in public at the UN General Assembly: reopening Hormuz within seven days in exchange for released frozen funds, an end to sanctions and the lifting of the US naval blockade, conditional on restarting nuclear talks.
27 Sep — Trump rejected Iran's offer and would not rule out renewed strikes, closing off the one path that would have relieved oil quickly.

28–29 Sep — Brent peaked near $108 a barrel on the 28th, the highest since the Strait of Hormuz was shut in February, then fell to about $100 on the 29th as regional exports recovered to 12.8 million barrels a day in September (roughly 20 million before the war). Iran meanwhile claimed fresh attacks on shipping and US Navy vessels.

29 Sep — New York Fed president John Williams said there is no urgency for another rate increase after September's hike. The market-implied probability of an October increase fell from 69.6% to 35.0% in a day.

2026-09-30.note: Brent near $100 a barrel is now only about 9% above where it sat a month ago, down from roughly 18-20% above at the $108 peak two days ago, and that compression is the whole of what reaches crypto from this. The route runs oil into headline inflation, headline inflation into the expected path of policy rates, and the rate path into the price of dollar liquidity — it is not a sentiment channel, and the dashboard does not treat it as one. Today you can watch the entire chain complete in a single number: the market-implied probability of an October Fed increase fell from 69.6% yesterday to 35.0% today, which lifted the L4 liquidity indicator out of negative territory and took the liquidity bucket from -100 to -70. The caution is that this is a repricing of expectations rather than of cash: the Treasury and the Fed's reverse repo facility are still draining dollars faster than at any point this month.
today: The oil war premium is unwinding in earnest. Brent settled near $100 a barrel on 29 September, down about 2.5% on the day and only around 9% above where it sat a month ago — against roughly 18–20% above a month ago when it peaked near $108 on the 28th. Bloomberg's 30 September market wrap has oil holding that loss, with Middle East exports now seen near pre-war levels. Supply is no longer arriving at a war price.

That fed straight through to the Fed, and it is the biggest single thing on the board today. New York Fed president John Williams said on 29 September that there is no urgency about another increase and no rush after September's hike, guiding towards just one more rise late in the year. The market-implied probability of an October increase fell from 69.6% to 35.0% in a day — the exact chain this section keeps describing, arriving in the one indicator that tracks it.

All four sub-scores still carry forward unchanged at Iran 4, Russia–Ukraine 3, risk of a new theatre 3 and headline density 3, for a total of 13 and an ELEVATED flag. The premium is coming out of the oil price, but the blockade is still in force, Trump's rejection of Iran's terms still stands and Iran is still claiming attacks on shipping, so the conflict itself has not de-escalated even though the market's pricing of it has.

lead: The score is +19 today, up from +11 ten sessions ago but down from +35 at the previous reading, because fund buying faded and two more indicators turned weaker.
bullets: Three indicators weakened, and the bitcoin fund revision explains most of it. Farside revised 7 October's bitcoin fund outflow to $485m from $277m, which alone lowers the earlier readings. On top of that, trading volume (coincident, bearish) turned negative with the past week's average at 0.81 times the 30-day average (below 0.85 scores negative), alternative-coin breadth (lagging, bearish) fell to 1 of 5 coins above their 50-day averages (2 or fewer scores negative), and the 20-day bitcoin fund total (coincident) dropped to neutral.

Price is still positive but cooling, and it is the lagging bucket. The price bucket is +67, down from +83. Bitcoin at $82,009 (part-day) is 5.7% above its 350-day average of $77,573, 14.1% above its 200-day average of $71,890 and 13.1% above its 100-day average of $72,506, and it is down 5.2% over five days.

Liquidity is unchanged at +27 and it is the leading bucket. The Treasury-plus-reverse-repo cash drain is $100.4bn lower than 20 sessions ago (below -$25bn scores positive) and the market-implied chance of an October Fed rate increase is 15.9%, under the 30% line. The drag is the dollar index, 2.0 points higher than 20 sessions ago (a rise of 1 point or more scores negative).

Price and liquidity still point the same way, but demand has turned against them. Demand is -36, down from +8, while price is +67 and liquidity is +27. The whole liquidity bucket is leading indicators and the whole price bucket is lagging ones, so the composite understates where liquidity points; today the drag comes instead from demand, which is coincident.

Fund buyers are leaving. The 20-day total into bitcoin funds is $1.93bn against $2bn needed (it was $2.09bn at the previous reading), and the past week's average daily flow is $167m below the past four weeks' average (a gap past $50m scores negative). Ethereum funds' 20-day total is $213m against $500m needed. Positioning is neutral at 0: the futures funding fee is +0.002% per eight hours (part-day), under the +0.005% bar, and open interest is down 8.4% over 5 days.

moves.t: It is 0.81 now (the past 7 days' average volume divided by the 30-day average). Above 0.85 the volume indicator goes from negative to neutral, lifting the composite from +19 to about +23.

moves.h: The bitcoin fund 20-day total climbs back above $2bn
moves.t: It is $1.93bn now, $75m short of the $2bn bar. Above it the fund indicator goes from neutral to positive and the composite from +19 to about +26.

moves.h: The dollar index gap to 20 sessions ago falls below 1 point
moves.t: It is 2.0 points higher now. Under 1 point the dollar indicator goes from negative to neutral, lifting the composite from +19 to about +30.

moves.h: Alternative-coin breadth rises to 3 of 5 coins above their 50-day averages
moves.t: It is 1 of 5 now. At 3 the breadth indicator goes from negative to neutral, lifting the composite from +19 to about +24.
